source_span: AI Credit Spreads (GSUCHS30) and hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) specifically are at the widest levels of the year. The last time spreads were nearly this high, the underlying equities were 15% lower... Translation: either the hyperscaler bond market is wrong, or hyperscaler stocks have another 15% to fall.
source_chain: Goldman's hyperscaler/data-center AI credit spreads have widened to their widest levels of the year (A), therefore because the last time spreads were this wide the same equities were 15% lower than today's price (B), therefore the bond market and stock market now disagree and one side must be wrong: either credit is overpricing the risk or hyperscaler equities have another 15% to fall (C). Invalidation (per the note's own framing): the bet that AI damage stays contained to credit only holds if credit stabilizes rather than equities catching down to it.
pulse_chain: Goldman's two AI credit baskets sit at their widest levels of the year (A), therefore because the last time debt traded this wide the same hyperscaler stocks were 15% lower than now (B), therefore that gap is the argument: either the bond market is wrong or those equities have another 15% to give (C). Invalidation: earnings this week (Meta Wednesday, 14% of the S&P reporting) settle which side is right, per JPMorgan's observation that earnings releases marked the prior wides in hyperscaler spreads.
why: The pulse reproduces Miller's A-therefore-B-therefore-C chain and its 15%-gap conclusion almost verbatim with correct attribution to Goldman's Louis Miller, and supplies an invalidation (earnings resolve the credit/equity disagreement) that is consistent with the gap's own logic and is itself correctly sourced to JPMorgan rather than misattributed to Miller.
